In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of technology assessments on health policy and health services, and the influence of health policy and health service decisions on technology assessment.
the impact of technology assessments by Australian advisory bodies on health care policy and practice.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the assessments have been influential, but the extent of influence is difficult to measure.
the assessments had a moderate effect on policy and practice.
the impact of assessments is difficult to measure, and that the impact of any single assessment is likely to be small, but that the impact of the overall assessment process is substantial.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the assessments had an impact on policy, although the effect was often less than might have been expected, and the impact of some assessments was unclear.

the influence of technology assessments on policy is limited, but that this influence can be enhanced by careful planning of the assessment and its presentation, by appropriate selection of technologies and by ensuring that the assessment is undertaken when the technology is being introduced.

technology assessments can influence health policy and practice, but that the effect is not always clear and is influenced by the context of policy development and the nature of the technology being assessed.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the influence of assessments is greatest when there is a need to justify the introduction of a new technology or to make a major change to existing practice, and where the assessment process is timely and provides new data.
the impact of technology assessments depends on the policy context in which they are undertaken.
the impact of technology assessments is not only determined by the quality of the assessment but also by other factors.
